item: The erase rewrites a plaintext main database in full after unlinking it and says the crypto-erase guarantee only for an encrypted one
summary: A main database known to be plaintext (head-only before: its body stayed on the disk), in the data folder or where DATABASE_URL keeps it, is checked against its identity read before anything is opened (lstat; gone, unidentifiable, a link or another file: never touched), each of its files opened no-follow, kept and unlinked at once, and at the very end of the erase rewritten in full through the kept handles over every data region (SEEK_DATA/SEEK_HOLE, else the logical size with the 64 MiB reserve; R797) after a fstat check, fsynced, the handles closed by the late pass after the pool (R789). Windows falls back to the first page then the unlink. Reported apart from Wiped n/n (report plaintext_store: overwritten, partially overwritten, not overwritten or first page, the reason, deleted, other names by count). _LIMIT_NOTE, the held-store note and the free-space overwrite's note claim the guarantee only for a main database known to be encrypted; plaintext and unknown fail closed with their own sentences (CLI, HTTP, panic page; strings x12). Hard-link witness tests in both locations and on the HTTP path; a stop mid-rewrite; a link swapped in at the path.
